note: The Statelessness Network Asia Pacific's summary of the Maldives' Citizenship Act: a Muslim who has lived in the Maldives continuously for at least twelve years may apply for citizenship, among other requirements (the Constitution admits no non-Muslim, which the game doesn't model); dual citizenship is permitted, with no conditions on a Maldivian taking another. Whether a foreigner naturalising must give up a prior citizenship isn't stated in what could be read, so it is null. Citizenship at birth is read from the same summary: the Citizenship Act gives citizenship automatically to a child born to a Maldivian citizen wherever the child is born (jus sanguinis); the summary states no citizenship by birth in the Maldives, so none is held. The summary also records differences between mothers and fathers in transmission depending on religion and marital status, which the form doesn't hold.

sources.title: Statelessness Network Asia Pacific (SEAP), Maldives – Laws
sources.said: A person may apply for Maldivian citizenship if they are Muslim and have resided in the Maldives for at least 12 years continuously among other requirements. ... Dual citizenship is permitted in the Maldives. There are no additional conditions imposed for Maldivian citizens to acquire dual citizenship. ... Citizenship legislation of the Maldives operates through jus sanguinis provisions that provide automatic citizenship to a child born to a citizen of the Maldives regardless of their place of birth. ... establish different conditions for women and men as regards the transmission of nationality depending, notably, on religion and marital status
